evidence:
REACHABILITY (passes): Every capability the brief asks for is reachable. Runtime: agent image is node:22-bookworm-slim with express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 under NODE_PATH (environment/Dockerfile lines 3-12), matching instruction.md line 13 'Server dependencies are already available' and integration.md lines 3-4; /instructions and /assets are COPYed (Dockerfile 14-15); polling/SSE/sockets are all allowed (hireops_rules.md line 123) so live updates need no extra package; restart_app is wired by tests/test.sh line 193 (APP_RESTART_HELPER) and functional judge.toml lines 14-18. The golden uses only express, better-sqlite3 and Node built-ins (package.json; src/db.js:7, src/index.js:16-18), and 20 scripted golden groups passed under uid 65534 with a real restart against hash-matched frozen bytes (results/workspace.json; index hashes verified). Seed supports every seed-dependent criterion: all 10 sign-in accounts in instruction.md line 17 exist in seed users; Noor's APP-101 has exactly 120 messages (long-thread paging 30/30/30/30); Lena's APP-301 has 3 messages, the 3rd from USR-REC3, with read_count 2 -> 1 unread by rules lines 151-153 and 205-207; candidate wording table and thread_page_size=30 are in the seed; APP-301 carries rejected_from/reject_reason for the privacy rules. Most rules are single-reading: one-stage moves, reopen-to-origin, interview cap incl. bulk and undo, board-order arrival (rules 89-92), undo scope including reopenings (rule 97 'restores a rejection reason that the move removed' forces reopen to be undoable), undo-once and later-move invalidation (rules 99-100), 401/403/404 (rules 21-23), unread/seen definitions (rules 151-166). The protocols in tests/scored/functional/prompt.md S/M/L/C/B are consistent with those rules under either reading of whether a re-order is itself an undoable move.

AMBIGUITY THAT FAILS A CONFORMING APP (the defect): hireops_rules.md lines 179-180 say a candidate sees 'a list of their own applications, each with the job title, the team and a status ... and the conversation for each', and instruction.md line 11 asks only for 'a simple applications view for candidates'. Showing/opening the candidate's conversation immediately is a reasonable reading, and under rules lines 151-158 a conversation that is open at its newest message is read, so its unread count is correctly 0. The functional grading assumes the other reading: prompt.md line 25 (protocol Z) 'Sign in as Lena Fischer ... read her unread count on her Product Designer conversation; the starting read markers give her 1. Do not open that conversation', and hro_unread_counts (weight 2, judge.toml lines 330-336) 'Lena Fischer starts with 1 unread on her conversation ... Fails if any count is wrong'. The reference itself takes the first reading: solution/app/public/js/threads.js line 220 'else if (candidate && threads().length === 1) open(threads()[0].id, false);' runs from shown() on the default candidate view (app.js setView line 98, called by render line 110); open() ends with markRead(id) (threads.js line 129), which zeroes a.unread client-side and POSTs /api/applications/:id/read (lines 100-108; server src/index.js 134-139, 418-421 persists last_read_id). Lena has exactly one application (APP-301), and keep.get('thread') is per-user localStorage (app.js 39-42) so it is empty in the judge's fresh independent context. Therefore signing in as Lena auto-opens her only conversation and marks it read on the server before the judge can comply with 'Do not open that conversation'; the judge is likely to observe 0 (the list-row badge is repainted to 0 immediately; the nav badge may briefly show 1 until the next render). The scripted golden evidence never signs in as Lena (grep of workspace.cjs for 'lena'/'CAN3' finds nothing), so this path is unmeasured. Run verdict: NOT EXERCISED (static trace only; no configured judge run exists per raw-evidence-index scope).

LOWER-RISK AMBIGUITIES (P3, reported as required by this row, not independently blocking): (a) Voluntary sign-out and reply drafts: instruction.md line 7 'get signed out' plus rules 170-175 'after the session ends' can be read as involuntary expiry only; a builder who clears reply drafts on an explicit Sign out (privacy reading) fails hro_pol_session_resume (weight 2.5), which requires Rafael's drafts to survive his own sign-out and Mei's visit. Rules 105-106 ('kept for that person on that browser until it is saved') and 170 ('belongs to that person ... on that browser') make persistence the stronger reading. (b) Stale-move replay: prompt.md line 17 defines a captured request as '(method, URL, body)'; an app that sends its card version in an If-Match header (allowed: rules 77-80 leave transport open, rules line 3-5 routes/fields are the builder's) could see the version dropped on replay; protocol C line 33 ('including whatever version or freshness value it sends ... exactly as it was sent') mitigates. The golden sends version in the JSON body (board.js 184-188). (c) Activity multi-card moves: hro_activity says 'each card of every single and multi-card move' has 'a readable line'; rules 110-113 only require each move recorded with what changed, so one line naming all cards is a conforming design a strict judge might fault; and 'naming who and the stages' for a re-ordering line goes slightly beyond rules' 'what changed'. (d) Anonymous 'board read' must be 401 (hro_anonymous); rules line 21 literally says 401 for any sessionless read, so a server-rendered board redirecting to /login is non-conforming by the letter, not a second reading. None of (a)-(d) is unreachable.

What the task does well: the runtime contract is explicit and consistent across instruction.md 13-15, integration.md and rules §8; seed values are deliberately chosen so every seed-dependent expectation is derivable from public rules; the judge prompt repeatedly allows UI-hidden refusals and route-agnostic discovery.
counterexample: A conforming app (the frozen golden itself) whose candidate view automatically opens a candidate's only conversation at its newest message, as allowed by hireops_rules.md lines 179-180 ('... and the conversation for each') and lines 151-158 (open at newest = read). When the judge signs in as Lena Fischer in protocol Z, threads.js line 220 opens APP-301 and markRead POSTs /api/applications/APP-301/read, so her count is 0 rather than the 1 the criterion requires; hro_unread_counts (weight 2) is scored 0 for a rule-conforming app, and the reference cannot meet its own Z expectation. Conversely, a broken app that never computes seeded read markers but happens to show the raw marker difference would be unaffected by this ambiguity; the check does not separate correct from incorrect on this path when the app auto-opens.
suggested_fix: Make the Lena reading independent of the view design: either remove the golden's single-application auto-open (threads.js line 220) and state in hireops_rules.md §7 that a candidate's conversation opens only when they choose it, or move the seeded-marker check to a candidate with two applications (Noor: APP-302 has one unread staff message) and/or let hro_unread_counts accept 0 when the app itself opened the conversation at its newest message; then rerun the golden through protocol Z. Optionally clarify in the brief that drafts persist across one's own sign-out.
